answer: Nine jurors grade each submission from 0 to 3. If any two scores differ by two or more, a second panel of five drawn from a rotating pool re-grades the case, and the side that loses the re-grade has its stake slashed. Each slash goes into an onyx public record with the submission hash, the score set and the wallet, so a bought jury can be traced afterwards instead of only suspected. A clean sheet is the opal that pays: 400 keys need 3,600 signed grades every epoch, and each one is a quartz shard of evidence the operator cannot retract once written.
